result.title: Lost in the Funnel: Selection-Induced Miscalibration in Ranking and Decision Systems
result.summary: Modern ranking and decision systems combine components with divergent objectives, and scores calibrated at the model boundary are used as calibrated probabilities throughout the funnel, across filtering, reranking, business-rule enforcement, and auctions. Yet calibration is typically validated only where the score is produced, so its breakdown where the score is used is routinely overlooked. We ask when calibration survives this selection, how inherited error differs from selection effects, and what can fail for a perfectly calibrated score at a component boundary. We study these questions through a boundary-wise diagnostic framework of residual identities. We target rubric-judged relevance rather than presentation-dependent metrics such as CTR, so calibration is measurable at every funnel layer of interest. We first present an industry-wide case study that applies our diagnosis to settings where calibration deteriorates at decision time, tracing the degradation to selection rather than model error. This diagnosis motivates Funnel-Aware Recalibration (FAR): post-hoc, selection-policy-aware recalibration at the boundary where scores drive decisions. In a live two-region production A/B test, FAR cuts decision-time expected calibration error (ECE) by 60-80% and improves auction efficiency. We further adapt two public datasets to simulate industry settings, providing additional evidence for the mechanism. We plan to release the adapted datasets and their generation pipeline to support further research. Finally, we distill these findings into practical operating principles for calibrating multi-stage scoring systems.

AI.brief_summary: 论文考察多阶段排序与决策漏斗中在模型边界标定好的分数经过筛选、重排和竞价后失去标定性的问题，提出基于残差恒等式的逐层诊断框架，并给出选择策略感知的后验重标定方法 FAR，在工业 A/B 测试和改造后的公开数据集上验证。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「选择而非模型误差导致标定退化、需在决策边界重新标定」的视角，可能可供核查 LVR 中多阶段证据筛选与停止决策的置信度标定问题，但本身不涉及视觉或 latent 推理机制。
